Set operations on tbl_gpu tables

Source: R/sets.R
set-ops.Rd

dplyr's row-set operations on GPU tables, run on the GPU:

  • union(): the distinct rows of x, in x's order, then the rows of y not already in x, in y's order.

  • union_all(): the rows of x (duplicates kept), then those of y.

  • intersect() and setdiff(): distinct rows of x, in x's order, that are (or are not) in y.

  • symdiff(): the rows of setdiff(x, y), then those of setdiff(y, x).

  • setequal(): TRUE or FALSE, ignoring row order and duplicates on both sides.

As in dplyr, x and y must have the same column names (the order may differ: y is reordered to x's), and each column must have a common type: logical, integer and double columns combine to the wider type, a logical or integer column with an integer64 one gives integer64 (integer64 and double have no common type: an error, as in dplyr), a Date and a POSIXct combine to POSIXct, two factors with different levels combine to a factor with the union of the levels, and a factor next to a character column gives a character column. A column-type mix that dplyr refuses (integer vs. character, factor vs. integer, ...) is an error naming the column and both types.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
union(x, y, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
union_all(x, y, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
intersect(x, y, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
setdiff(x, y, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
symdiff(x, y, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
setequal(x, y, ...)

Arguments

x, y

tbl_gpu objects. y may also be a plain data.frame (uploaded automatically via tbl_gpu()) – unlike the join verbs, these generics have no copy= argument.

...

Not used; must be empty (dplyr itself requires this too).

Value

A tbl_gpu with x's column order and grouping, with the rows in the order described above, except setequal(), which returns TRUE or FALSE.

Details

These run in dplyr on the CPU: tables with duplicated column names; a Date column next to a POSIXct column in a zone other than UTC (the Date becomes local midnight of that zone); a column with element names or a one-column matrix column, which dplyr combines by its own rules (except in setequal()); and a rowwise x.
